page.description: ChromeOS Flex editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: Google's ChromeOS build for ordinary PCs and Macs: a browser-first desktop that is installed from a USB stick prepared with Google's own recovery utility rather than from a downloadable ISO.
pros: Runs ChromeOS on generic x86_64 hardware instead of a Chromebook.
Managed through the Google Admin console like other ChromeOS devices.
Fast boot and automatic background updates.
Free, and boots from the same account as other ChromeOS devices.
cons: No direct ISO: the image is written only by the Chromebook Recovery Utility, so ROMinit cannot pin or prepare it.
Certified hardware list is limited; unsupported machines lose sound, Wi-Fi or graphics.
Installing replaces the existing system on the target disk.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for ChromeOS Flex; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Google's flow: install the Chromebook Recovery Utility extension, let it download the image for your model, write it to a USB stick, then boot the target PC from it. The utility writes and erases the stick; installing ChromeOS Flex erases the target disk.
